newsitem.title: USA: Ampace calls 1997 "transitional year" for profits.
newsitem.headline: Ampace calls 1997 "transitional year" for profits.

text.p: Ampace Corp said Monday that its expects to complete several more acquisitions during 1997 and to experience significant internal growth, after reporting a loss for 1996.

The company said that it sees 1997 as a "transitional year" for profits as it sees the benefits of cost-restructuring and the addition of new and better freight from its business development activities.
The company, an acquisition-holding company, went public in Feb, 1995, to purchase small and medium-sized truckload carriers. It reported a loss of $400,000, or $0.14 a share,
in the fourth quarter of 1996, on revenues of $7.9 million. In the year-earlier period the company reported a loss of $300,000 ($0.09) on revenues of $6.3 million.
For all of 1996 the loss was $876,000 ($0.29 a share) on revenues of $30.4 million, as opposed to a loss of $238,000 ($0.09) on revenues of $21.2 million in 1995.
Ampace said it is on track with its original five-year plan, which identifies structural development with an emphasis on growth as the first priority in the first thre years.
